title: Back the Companion transport with fetch and harden the executor for real responses

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0082 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-25 directive 'dale a lo que sigue' (ultracode on) — the fourth slice of the REQ-INT-002 Companion adapter, stacked on the unmerged CHG-0081 branch, making the command transport real over HTTP. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0082.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors, SPEC-0001 REQ-INT-002 / US-010 AC-018, and the 2026-08-25 user directive.

claims.statement: createFetchTransport(fetchImpl) backs a ControlApiTransport with a fetch implementation, declared against a structural FetchLike type so the package needs no DOM or Node fetch type dependency. The transport reads the response body as text and never parses it, so a non-JSON body does not throw inside the transport. A real-HTTP round-trip test stands up a local http.Server and drives the built request through the global fetch, asserting the received method, path, Bearer header, and body and the parsed applied outcome.
claims.evidence: companion/src/transport.ts createFetchTransport and FetchLike; companion/tests/fetchTransport.contract.test.ts (real http.Server round-trip).

claims.statement: An adversarial review workflow (five independent lenses — robustness, contract-fidelity, correctness, security, test-adequacy — each finding verified by a separate refutation agent, 22 agents total) surfaced that the executor introduced in CHG-0081 was not robust once driven by a real fetch transport. Three distinct real defects were confirmed and fixed: JSON.parse on the response body was unguarded, so a non-JSON or empty body (a proxy or gateway error page, a dropped connection) threw a SyntaxError instead of the promised typed failure; a fetch rejection (host down, DNS, connection refused) propagated as an unhandled throw rather than a CommandFailure; and a 2xx envelope without a command returned { ok: true, outcome: undefined } instead of failing. An injected stub never produces these — only a real transport does — which is why the review was run before finalizing.
claims.evidence: the CHG-0082 review workflow result (9 confirmed findings collapsing to these three defects); companion/src/transport.ts executeVisibilityCommand before hardening.

claims.statement: executeVisibilityCommand now returns a typed CommandFailure for each failure mode: a transport rejection becomes { ok: false, status: 0, code: NETWORK_ERROR }; a non-JSON or empty body becomes { ok: false, status, code: MALFORMED_RESPONSE }; a 2xx without a command falls through to the failure return; and a non-2xx JSON body without an error object falls back to code UNKNOWN. Six tests were added covering each path, including a real refused-connection round-trip, so no failure mode escapes as a throw.

This is still not a runnable Companion module: no InstanceBase, button callbacks, connection configuration, or retry/backoff. The Companion module packaging, the AC-018 state-feedback half, and the Take/trigger catalog extension remain deferred (.frontier nodes companion-adapter-runtime-module, companion-adapter-feedback, companion-catalog-take-trigger-actions). Additive to the @overlaykit/companion package; no server, protocol, or Studio source changed.
claims.evidence: companion/src (no InstanceBase or retry); the .frontier companion nodes.

claims.statement: Human review accepted CHG-0082: createFetchTransport backs the transport with a real fetch (proven over an http.Server round-trip), and executeVisibilityCommand — hardened after an adversarial review workflow caught three real defects only a real transport exposes (unguarded JSON.parse, unhandled fetch rejection, malformed 2xx) — now degrades every failure mode to a typed CommandFailure. The runnable Companion module, AC-018 feedback, and Take/trigger catalog extension remain deferred as .frontier nodes.
claims.evidence: companion/src/transport.ts and companion/tests/fetchTransport.contract.test.ts; the CHG-0082 review workflow result; npm run check, the CHG-0082 pull-request Constitution run (8 jobs green), and human acceptance on 2026-08-25.

successCriteria.statement: The fetch-backed transport carries a built command to a real HTTP endpoint and the applied outcome is returned.
successCriteria.verification: companion/tests/fetchTransport.contract.test.ts round-trips through a local http.Server via the global fetch and asserts the received request and the applied outcome.

successCriteria.statement: Every failure mode — network rejection, non-JSON or empty body, malformed success, and error-object-less non-2xx — becomes a typed CommandFailure, never a throw.
successCriteria.verification: Tests assert typed failures with status 0 / NETWORK_ERROR, MALFORMED_RESPONSE, a failed 2xx-without-command, and the UNKNOWN fallback.

successCriteria.statement: No existing behavior regresses and the adapter stays dependency-isolated.
successCriteria.verification: npm run check and npm run build pass across all workspaces; companion depends only on @overlaykit/protocol and needs no fetch type dependency.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0082 records the fetch transport, the adversarial-review findings, and the executor hardening before implementation of the record.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.
